issues.legal_issue: Acquisition of land for an existing public facility is not a colourable exercise of eminent-domain power merely because the State had encroached on the land and was subject to a civil injunction concerning it.
material_facts: Land included in an existing public works office compound had been found by a civil court to belong to the respondent and to have been encroached upon by the State.
The civil court ordered removal of the compound wall and restoration of possession, and the State had appealed that decision.
The State initiated acquisition of the encroached land so that it could remain part of the public office compound.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was for a public purpose and was not a colourable or arbitrary exercise of power; the acquisition notification and declaration were valid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 permits acquisition for a public purpose. The State may exercise eminent-domain power to acquire land needed for an existing public facility. In these circumstances, the fact that the State disputed the civil court’s finding and appealed the injunction did not make the acquisition colourable; resort to acquisition implied recognition of the respondent’s title to the extent found by the civil court. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and existing_public_facility and civil_court_found_encroachment_and_ownership and injunction_required_removal_and_restitution and acquisition_sought_to_retain_land_for_facility

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.existing_public_facility: The land was being used as part of an existing public facility.
predicates.civil_court_found_encroachment_and_owner: A civil court found that the government had encroached on land belonging to the private owner.
predicates.injunction_required_removal_and_restitut: A civil court ordered the government to remove the encroachment and restore possession to the owner.
predicates.acquisition_sought_to_retain_land_for_fa: The government sought to acquire the land so it could continue using it for the public facility.

issues.definition: When land is being acquired for an existing public facility and the government seeks to retain land that a civil court found it had encroached upon and ordered it to restore, the acquisition is treated as a valid public-purpose acquisition rather than a colourable exercise.

issues.legal_issue: Urgency provisions may be used to dispense with an opportunity to object where an injunction requires removal of a structure needed to secure an existing public facility.
material_facts: A civil court had ordered the State to demolish the compound wall and restore possession of the land.
The wall was needed to protect the existing public works office building.
The acquisition was intended to retain the land for that public purpose, and the matters ordinarily addressed in an objection inquiry were redundant in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The government was justified in invoking the urgency power and dispensing with the inquiry into objections.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 17(1) and 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 permit the urgency procedure, including dispensing with the inquiry under Section 5A, where the circumstances establish urgency. Here, the injunction requiring demolition and restitution, together with the need to retain the wall to secure the existing public office, made the usual inquiry issues redundant. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The government initiated a proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.injunction_required_removal_and_restitut: A civil court ordered the government to remove the encroachment and restore possession to the owner.
predicates.compound_wall_needed_for_public_facility: The structure on the land was needed to protect an existing public facility.
predicates.delay_would_threaten_retention_of_facili: Complying with the injunction without urgent acquisition would prevent the government from retaining the land and structure needed for the public facility.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding concerns land subject to an order requiring removal and restitution, and delay would jeopardize a structure needed to secure an existing public facility, dispensing with the objection inquiry is justified.
